sentences.text: Bench: P.Sam Koshy, N.Tukaramji  THE HON'BLE SRI JUSTICE P.SAM KOSHY  AND  THE HON'BLE SRI JUSTICE N.TUKARAMJI  WRIT PETITION NO.12422 OF 2012 ORDER:
(per Hon'ble Sri Justice P.SAM KOSHY) Heard Sri A.Ramakrishna Reddy, learned Standing Counsel for Insurance Company appearing for the petitioner and perused the record.

2. The instant Writ Petition has been filed challenging the Award dated 09.11.2011 in O.P.No.213 of 2010 on the file of Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal (Additional/District Judge) at Mahabubnagar,
filed under Section 163-A of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 whereby the matter was settled in Lok Adalat for an amount of Rs.3,24,000/- as compensation in favour of claimants.

entities.text: Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal (Additional/District Judge) at Mahabubnagar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3. Subsequent to the matter settled in Lok Adalat on 09.11.2011, the petitioner-insurance company filed the present Writ Petition after about six (6) months i.e., on 24.04.2012 challenging the Award dated 09.11.2011 passed by the Lok Adalat on the ground that there was misrepresentation and mischief played by respondent Nos.1 to 3 - claimants in filing the claim petition.

According to learned Standing Counsel for insurance company, the mischief and misrepresentation were to the extent that a fabricated cover note was produced along with claim petition and on the basis of which, compensation was sought.

He also contended that without proper verification of the said cover note, under bona fide impression, counsel for the insurance company before MACT as well as the Officer from the insurance company believed that the cover note produced by the claimants is to be genuine and agreed for settlement of the matter before Lok Adalat and an amount of Rs.3,34,000/- was awarded as compensation to the claimants.
5.

Now, the contention of leaned Standing Counsel for the petitioner-insurance company is that subsequent to the matter getting settled before Lok Adalat, it was learnt that the said cover note produced by the claimants was not genuine as there was implication of dates made by the claimants and thereafter the insurance company filed the present Writ Petition.

sentences.text: The Award is of the year 2011.
Today, we are in 2024 i.e, more than 13 years have been passed.
In between PSK,J&NTR,J wp_12422_2012 by way of interim order of this Court, 50% of the amount Awarded has already been deposited and the said amount has been disbursed to the claimants.

As such at this juncture, the amount of compensation left to be paid to the claimants is nearly Rs.1,62,000/-.
7.

The fact which needs to be appreciated at this juncture is that undoubtedly, the counsel representing the insurance company before the MACT was engaged by the Authorized Officer of the insurance company.
The other admitted fact is that the claim petition got stood after the matter was referred to Lok Adalat for settlement.

In the course of settlement, the Officer of the insurance company and the counsel for the insurance company were all present and therefore, it is to be presumed that the Officer and also the counsel had agreed for the matter to be settled after due verification of facts.
The impugned Award dated 09.11.2011 would also show that it was signed by the Authorized Officer of the insurance company and also the counsel representing the insurance company.
8. In view of the above, the interference of the impugned Award now after so long period does not seem to be PSK,J&NTR,J wp_12422_2012 justifiable any further.
We do not find any strong case made out calling for interference of the impugned Award.
Thus, the writ petition stands disposed of.
The balance compensation amount, if any due by petitioner-insurance company, the same shall be deposited within a period of six (6) weeks.
There shall be no order as to costs.
Miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending in this writ petition shall stand closed.

_______________ JUSTICE N.TUKARAMJI Date: 12.08.2024 YVL Oriental Insurance Company ... vs Kum.Haleema Begum on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137177055/
